news.hook: Alfred Collins was set for a breakout year on the 49ers' defensive line when a practice mishap in Australia changed everything. The promising young tackle now faces a full recovery ahead of the team's historic opener Down Under.
news.name: 49ers DT Alfred Collins Tears Patellar Tendon, Out for 2026 Season
news.summary: The San Francisco 49ers lost defensive tackle Alfred Collins to a torn patellar tendon during Tuesday's practice in Melbourne, ruling him out for the entire 2026 season. Drafted 43rd overall in 2025 out of Texas, the 24-year-old rookie from last year had tallied 17 tackles, a sack, two forced fumbles, and two recoveries—including a key goal-line play in an overtime win over the Rams. Coming off shoulder surgery, his absence adds to the front's woes with other injuries like those to Ricky Pearsall and Sam Okuayinonu, forcing reliance on CJ West, Gracen Halton, and others as they prep for Thursday's season opener against the Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Nick Bosa, back from his own ACL tear, encouraged Collins to take it one day at a time.

news.hook: Pittsburgh Steelers veteran Cam Heyward didn't hold back at a press conference, labeling the NFL's franchise tag 'stupid' as the team races to extend cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
news.name: Cam Heyward Calls NFL Franchise Tag Stupid Amid Joey Porter Jr. Talks
news.summary: Heyward, a 16-year veteran and NFL Players Association executive, criticized the tag for giving teams leverage over players, especially stars like Porter who enters the final year of his rookie deal. With the Steelers' self-imposed deadline nearing before their season opener against Atlanta, a tag next year could pay Porter around $21 million—far below market rates like Christian Gonzalez's $33.75 million average. Heyward stressed that top players deserve top pay in their short careers, while reactions split between fans defending the CBA system and others noting players' long-standing frustration.

news.hook: Hours before kickoff at Lumen Field, injuries sidelined key players on both teams, forcing quick calls from the coaching staffs to keep their Super Bowl rematch plans on track.
news.name: Patriots and Seahawks Tweak Rosters for Super Bowl Rematch Opener
news.summary: The Seahawks ruled out safety Nick Emmanwori with an ankle injury, listing him inactive alongside wide receiver Tory Horton, safety Ty Okada, guard Beau Stephens, defensive end Mike Morris, tight end Nick Kallerup, and emergency QB Jalen Milroe. They signed safety AJ Finley and elevated Rodney Thomas II to cover the thin secondary. The Patriots sat running back TreVeyon Henderson due to his ankle issue, elevating RB Lan Larison and punter Mitch Wishnowsky for backfield and special teams depth. These moves highlight how injuries reshaped both rosters right before their season opener.
